questions.question: A 3-neighbor classifier sees labels [cat, cat, dog] among the nearest points. What label does majority voting return?
options: A continuous average of the two labels
No label until a neural network is trained
questions.explanation: Two of the three neighbors are cats, so an unweighted majority vote returns cat.

questions.question: A dataset combines age (0-100) with annual income (0-200000). Why can raw Euclidean KNN be misleading?
options: Euclidean distance ignores every numeric feature
KNN always converts regression targets into classes
Large values make every pair of points equally close
Income differences can dominate the distance because its numeric scale is much larger
questions.explanation: The feature with the larger unit range contributes more to squared distance. Scaling puts features on comparable ranges.

questions.question: Vectors [1,1,0] and [2,2,0] point in the same direction. What is their cosine similarity?
questions.explanation: Cosine similarity ignores magnitude; positive multiples in the same direction have similarity 1.

questions.question: Why can a KD-tree lose its speed advantage as the number of features grows?
options: The tree can only store binary labels
Many regions cannot be pruned, so searches approach brute force
Higher dimensions make L1 distance undefined
KD-trees require a neural-network embedding first
questions.explanation: In high dimensions, points become hard to separate with axis-aligned bounds; many branches remain candidates.

questions.question: A KNN regressor finds target values [10,14,16] with equal weights. What prediction does it make?
questions.explanation: The equal-weight regression prediction is the mean: (10+14+16)/3=13.33.

questions.question: How should you choose K for a new KNN classifier?
options: Always choose K=1 because it has the lowest training error
Choose K equal to the number of features
Pick the largest K without checking class proportions
Compare candidate values on validation data after fitting the feature scaling on the training split
questions.explanation: Validation compares the bias-variance tradeoff. K=1 can memorize noise, while an overly large K washes out local structure.
